items.title: Ellis Marsalis interviewed by Monk Rowe, New Orleans, Louisiana, January 7, 2020
items.q: the biggest studio was probably Allen Toussaint’s studio at Sea-Saint. And Allen was the piano player.

ctx.x: Did you get in on any of the recording work that happened, a couple of the studios in New Orleans? Like recording sessions. You’d just get a call to come down and —

Very few. Most of the rhythm & blues sessions were done, the biggest studio was probably Allen Toussaint’s studio at Sea-Saint. And Allen was the piano player. And there were sessions where he would call somebody, like Eddie Bo, who was a piano player. And then there was James Booker. He would get James Booker and he was also a piano player. So I was never called to do any of that. I remember talking to Dave Bartholomew one time, I said, “Man, look, I need a gig.” He said, “Oh man, you don’t need no job.” Well…

items.title: Allen Toussaint Interview, 1979-03-13
items.q: Like Ellis and myself, of course.

ctx.x: Do you listen to any of the jazz groups in town?
Seven, nine. Like Ellis and myself, of course.

And James Rivers is doing some really good things again. Yes, yes. He's so authentic. Frank Butler. Well, thank you very much, Alan Toussaint. It's been a real pleasure and a real honor having you here with our WTUL audience.
